key_insight: SpeechParaling-Bench provides the first large-scale, fine-grained benchmark for paralinguistic-aware speech generation, expanding feature coverage from under 50 to over 100 and supplying a >1,000-sample English–Chinese parallel corpus to enable consistent evaluation of LALMs.
problem_solved: Existing evaluations of paralinguistic capabilities in large audio-language models are coarse and inconsistent, and they struggle with subjective assessment—SpeechParaling-Bench fills this gap with richer feature coverage and standardized cross-lingual data.
method: Define and expand a fine-grained paralinguistic taxonomy to cover >100 features (e.g., prosody, emotion, emphasis, speaking rate, voice quality).
Curate a >1,000-sample English–Chinese parallel speech dataset annotated for the expanded paralinguistic features to support cross-lingual benchmarking.
Introduce a standardized evaluation protocol combining structured human ratings and objective measures to reduce subjectivity and enable reproducible comparison of LALMs.
impact: This benchmark enables more precise, reproducible assessment of paralinguistic behavior in speech-generating models, accelerating development of natural, expressive LALMs and improving cross-lingual evaluation practices.
visual_elements: Bar chart comparing feature coverage: <50 (prior) vs >100 (SpeechParaling-Bench).
Pipeline diagram: taxonomy → parallel dataset (EN–ZH) → annotation → evaluation protocol.
Sample waveform + spectrogram annotated with paralinguistic labels (pitch, intensity, emotion) to illustrate fine-grained annotations.
Heatmap or radar chart showing model performance across selected paralinguistic features (intelligibility, prosody, emotion, emphasis).
paper_title: SpeechParaling-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Paralinguistic-Aware Speech Generation
paper_authors: Ruohan Liu, Shukang Yin, Tao Wang, Dong Zhang, Weiji Zhuang
